q: What is the nightlife like in Bihać?
a: Nightlife in Bihać is relaxed and mostly takes place in cafés and bars in the centre and along the Una river, while there are few proper nightclubs. In summer the town is much livelier thanks to festivals, open-air concerts and the Una Regatta. If you are after big clubs open until dawn, Bihać is not Zagreb, but there is plenty of choice for a pleasant evening with music.

q: Where do people go out in the evening in Bihać?
a: In the evening, people in Bihać mostly head to the town centre, the streets around the old quarter and the terraces along the Una. That is where you will find cafés, pubs and bars with music, and it is busiest at weekends. In summer part of the evening scene moves to the riverbank and to the places where open-air concerts are held.

q: Are there cafés by the Una river in Bihać?
a: Yes, along the Una in Bihać itself there is a row of cafés with terraces right on the riverbank, and sitting over coffee by the river is one of the favourite local pastimes. The terraces are full from morning to evening, especially from spring to autumn. If you stay in one of our apartments in the centre, the river is just a few minutes' walk away.

q: Are there nightclubs in Bihać?
a: Bihać has only a handful of nightclubs and bars with DJs, and what is on offer changes from season to season. Most young people go out at weekends to bars in the centre that stay open late. For current venues and events, it is best to follow local social media or ask your host.

q: What time do cafés and bars close in Bihać?
a: Cafés in Bihać are usually open from morning until late evening, and some stay open longer at weekends and in summer. Bars and clubs have extended opening hours, especially on Fridays and Saturdays. Exact hours depend on the venue and on town regulations, so check locally.

q: What is the Bihać Summer festival (Bihaćko ljeto)?
a: Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer) is a performing arts festival in Bihać that runs for about two weeks at the end of June and the beginning of July. The programme includes theatre performances, including shows for children, concerts, exhibitions and film screenings. The festival has been held for almost three decades, and the dates for the current year are announced by the Bihać Cultural Centre (Kulturni centar Bihać) and the City of Bihać.

q: When is the Una Regatta?
a: The International Tourist Una Regatta takes place every summer, usually in the second half of July, and lasts about four days. In 2026 it was held from 22 to 25 July, as the 52nd edition. Check the exact dates for next year on the official channels of the organiser and the City of Bihać, as they change from year to year.

q: What is the Una Regatta?
a: The Una Regatta is a multi-day descent of the Una river in boats and rafts, with a long tradition and more than fifty editions. The route usually starts near Martin Brod, passes through Una National Park and Bihać, and finishes downstream towards Bosanska Krupa. Alongside the descent, concerts and get-togethers are held in Bihać on those days, so the town is full of visitors.

q: Can tourists take part in the Una Regatta?
a: Yes, the Una Regatta is open to tourists and recreational paddlers, not just professional rowers. Participants register with the organiser, and the conditions, equipment and price are published before each edition. If you are planning to come then, book your accommodation early, as it is the busiest week in Bihać; you can send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Do I need to book accommodation in Bihać early for the Una Regatta?
a: Yes, during the Una Regatta and other summer events in July, accommodation in Bihać fills up quickly, so booking a few weeks in advance is a good idea. With us, you send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com with your dates and number of guests, and the owner confirms availability within 12 hours. You pay in cash on arrival, and if you pay a deposit in advance you get a discount.

q: Are there concerts in Bihać in summer?
a: Yes, several open-air concerts are held in Bihać in summer, as part of the Bihać Summer festival, other summer festivals and the Una Regatta. Concerts often take place by the river and in the town centre, and some are free. The programme is published afresh each year, so keep an eye on the City of Bihać website and local media.

q: What festivals take place in Bihać?
a: The best known are the Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer) performing arts festival at the end of June and beginning of July and the International Tourist Una Regatta in July. In recent years there have also been summer music festivals and a film festival dedicated to adventure and nature. The names and dates of smaller festivals change, so check them before your trip.

q: Is Bihać a good place for young people to go out?
a: Bihać is appealing for young people mainly in summer, when there are festivals, concerts, the Una Regatta and rafting. Nights out are more laid-back and cheaper than in bigger cities, and socialising happens in cafés, bars and by the river. Groups of friends often combine rafting during the day with a night out in town.

q: How much is a drink in a bar in Bihać?
a: Drink prices in Bihać are lower than in Croatia: a beer in a café usually costs a few KM, and a cocktail a little more. Exact prices depend on the venue, its location and the type of drink. As a rough guide, expect a night out here to be noticeably cheaper than on the Croatian coast.

q: Is Bihać safe at night?
a: Bihać is generally a quiet town, and walking through the centre and along the Una in the evening is normal even for families. The usual precautions apply: watch your belongings in crowds, do not leave valuables in the car and stick to well-lit streets. In an emergency, the police number is 122 and ambulance is 124.

q: How do I get a taxi home at night in Bihać?
a: Taxi companies in Bihać can be booked by phone, and there are taxi ranks in the centre. Agree the fare before the journey or ask for the meter to be switched on, especially for trips out of town. If you are staying in a house on the Una in Lohovo or Grmuša, ask your host for the number of a reliable taxi, as at night it is better to book in advance.

q: Is there Uber or Bolt in Bihać?
a: Ride-hailing apps such as Bolt or Uber are not reliably available in Bihać, so do not count on them as your only option. It is safer to use local taxi companies that you book by phone. Before your trip, open the app and check whether it currently works in Bihać.

q: How much is a taxi from Bihać centre to Lohovo?
a: Lohovo is about 10 km from the centre of Bihać, so a taxi ride usually takes around 15 minutes, and the price depends on the company and time of day. It is best to agree the fare before setting off or ask for the meter to be switched on. Your host in Lohovo can recommend a taxi that guests have already used.

q: Can I walk back to my apartment in Bihać centre at night?
a: If you are staying in an apartment in the centre of Bihać, most cafés and bars are a few minutes' walk away, so getting home on foot is easy. The centre is well lit and there are people about in the evening, especially in summer. This is one of the reasons younger guests choose our apartments in the centre, such as Apartman Centar or LUX Apartments Bihać.

q: Are there pubs with live music in Bihać?
a: Yes, a few bars and pubs in Bihać occasionally have live music, usually at weekends. Styles range from rock and pop to folk music, depending on the venue. Programmes are posted on the venues' social media, so check them the week before you arrive. Entry is usually free or a token amount.

q: Where are open-air concerts held in Bihać in summer?
a: Summer concerts in Bihać are often held by the river, at town venues such as Gradska ada (the town river island) and in the town centre. The location depends on the organiser and the festival. Follow the official websites of the City of Bihać and the Bihać Cultural Centre for the current schedule. For bigger concerts, arrive early because of parking.

q: Is there a cinema or theatre in Bihać?
a: Yes, Bihać has a cultural centre that hosts theatre performances, concerts and film screenings, and in summer the programme is particularly full thanks to the Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer) festival. The programme changes, so check the Bihać Cultural Centre website. Performances are mostly in Bosnian, Croatian or Serbian.

q: What is a typical evening like in Bihać?
a: A typical summer evening in Bihać starts with a stroll along the Una and a coffee or ice cream on a terrace, continues with dinner at a restaurant and ends with a drink in one of the bars in the centre. The town is not large, so you can get everywhere on foot. At weekends the atmosphere is livelier, on weekdays calmer.

q: Can you smoke in cafés in Bihać, and are there non-smoking places?
a: Smoking in cafés is still more common in Bosnia and Herzegovina than in most EU countries, so indoor spaces are often smoky. In summer this is less of a problem, as people sit on terraces by the river. If smoke bothers you, ask whether the venue has a separate non-smoking area.

q: What can I do in the evening in Bihać if I don't like nightlife?
a: If you are not keen on noisy nights out, enjoy an evening walk along the Una, dinner at a riverside restaurant or a quiet evening on the terrace of a house by the river. Many of our guests choose cottages in Lohovo, Pritoka or Grmuša precisely for the peace, a barbecue in the garden and the sound of the river. In summer you can also catch a Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer) theatre performance.

q: Is Bihać good for a stag or hen party?
a: Bihać is a good choice for a stag or hen party if you like a mix of adventure and socialising: rafting during the day, then dinner and a night out in town. Groups usually choose a house or villa on the Una with a garden and barbecue. For group accommodation, send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com or via WhatsApp/Viber on +387 61 591 320.

q: Can we play loud music at holiday houses on the Una?
a: The holiday houses on the Una are in quiet villages where neighbours live too, so guests are expected to respect house rules at night and not play loud music. It is customary to turn music down outdoors after 10 or 11 pm. Your host will explain the rules of the individual property on arrival.

q: When are the most events in Bihać?
a: Bihać has the most events in July, when Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer), summer concerts and the Una Regatta overlap. June and August are also lively thanks to tourists and rafting. Outside the season the town is quieter, but cafés and restaurants are open all year round. So book accommodation for July in good time.

q: Is there anything to do in the evening in Bihać in winter?
a: In winter Bihać is quieter, but cafés, restaurants and bars are open all year, and the cultural centre has a theatre and concert programme. In December there are usually festive New Year events in town. For a cosy winter evening, many people choose a heated house on the Una and dinner at a restaurant.

q: How can I celebrate New Year's Eve in Bihać?
a: You can see in the New Year in Bihać at an outdoor public celebration if the town organises one, at a restaurant with a New Year's menu or in a rented house with friends. Restaurants usually require booking in advance for New Year's Eve. For New Year accommodation, send your enquiry early, as larger houses are booked up quickly.

q: Are there sports bars in Bihać to watch football?
a: Yes, Bihać has cafés and pubs with big screens showing football and other sports, especially during major tournaments. Some also have pool or darts. For big matches, arrive early as seats fill up quickly.

q: Is alcohol available in Bihać?
a: Yes, alcohol is served in most cafés, bars and restaurants in Bihać and sold in shops. Although the population is predominantly Muslim, social life is open and relaxed. If you want a local beer, order Preminger from the Bihać brewery. Local rakija (fruit brandy) is also commonly drunk with a meal.

q: Are people in Bihać friendly to foreigners?
a: People in Bihać are as a rule hospitable and open towards visitors, and many younger locals speak English, while some older people speak German. In cafés and restaurants you will easily get a recommendation or help. Our team and the property owners speak Bosnian, English and German.

q: Can you swim in the Una at night?
a: We do not recommend swimming in the Una at night, as the water is cold, the current is strong in places and you cannot see rocks or depth in the dark. The Una is a relatively cold river even in summer. Swim during the day, at known bathing spots and with company, and enjoy the river from the bank in the evening.

q: Is Bihać safe for women travelling alone?
a: Bihać is generally considered a quiet town, and women travelling alone do not usually report any particular problems. The usual precautions apply: at night, stick to well-lit, busier streets and use a reliable taxi. Apartments in the centre are a practical choice, as everything is within walking distance.

q: What are the police and ambulance numbers in Bihać?
a: In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the police number is 122, the fire brigade 123 and emergency medical services 124. The European emergency number 112 also works, but using the local numbers is recommended. Save them in your phone before going out, especially if you are heading out of town at night.

q: Can I cycle around Bihać in the evening?
a: Yes, the centre of Bihać is flat and well suited to cycling, and there are lovely stretches along the Una for an evening ride. At night, always use lights and reflective gear, as there are not cycle lanes everywhere and you will share part of the road with cars. For rides towards Lohovo and Grmuša, go in daylight.

q: Is there an open-air cinema in Bihać in summer?
a: In summer, open-air film screenings are occasionally held in Bihać, as part of festivals or the town's summer programme, and some camps on the Una have their own open-air cinema. Dates change every year. Follow the Bihać Cultural Centre programme and local announcements.

q: Where is the best place to stay in Bihać for going out?
a: For going out, it is best to stay in the centre of Bihać, as cafés, bars and restaurants are within walking distance and you will not need a taxi. Our apartments in the centre, such as Apartman City Centar, Farah Superior Apartments or Feel Luxury Apartments, are well suited to this. A whole apartment with us costs from 25 € (50 KM) per night, roughly what a single room for one person costs in Bihać.

q: Is Bihać quiet enough for a relaxing holiday, or too noisy in summer?
a: Even in summer Bihać is mostly quiet, with noise limited to the town centre at weekends and during festivals. If you want complete peace, choose a house on the Una in Lohovo or Grmuša, where evenings pass to the sound of the river. If you want to be close to the nightlife, choose an apartment in the centre.
